Kutlerri.ai Raises $4 Mn to Scale AI Agents for Restaurant Businesses
Om Singh
| November 13 | Business Stories , Funding Feed
Share
Houston and Bhubaneswar-based startup Kutlerri.ai has raised $4 million in funding from Houston-based Narahari Investments as it looks to expand its artificial intelligence solutions for restaurant businesses.
The fresh capital will support the expansion of its AI Catering Sales Agent, the launch of three additional AI agents currently in beta testing, and the development of a mobile-first self-service application for restaurant operators, the startup said in a press release.
Founded in December 2025 by Kiran Rana and Payal Tripathy , Kutlerri.ai is developing AI-powered tools to help restaurants generate more sales, control operating expenses and improve profitability. Ankit Narain and Rishabh Srivastav are also part of the founding team.
Unlike conventional software providers that charge fixed subscription fees, Kutlerri.ai follows a performance-linked pricing model. Restaurants are charged based on the additional revenue generated or costs saved through its products.
AI Agent Helps Restaurants Find Catering Customers
Kutlerri.ai’s first commercially available product, the AI Catering Sales Agent, focuses on helping restaurants grow their catering businesses.
The agent identifies potential catering customers within a 30-mile radius of a restaurant and reaches out to them through emails, text messages and phone calls. It also helps restaurants convert incoming enquiries into catering orders.
The product was developed in collaboration with RASA, a five-location fast-casual restaurant group operating in the Washington DC region.
According to Kutlerri.ai, its AI agent helped RASA generate $450,000 in additional catering revenue over a 10-month period. The startup said the revenue was more than 10 times the amount RASA paid for the service, without requiring the restaurant group to hire additional sales personnel.
Plans to Expand Product Portfolio and Team
Kutlerri.ai currently has one commercially available product, three AI agents undergoing beta testing and two more in development.
The latest funding will help the company accelerate product development, expand its teams and bring additional AI-powered solutions to restaurant operators.
The startup has more than 10 signed customers in the US, which remains its primary market. Its product development and engineering operations are based in Bhubaneswar, while it also maintains an office in Houston.
Alongside its US expansion, Kutlerri.ai is exploring business opportunities in India and other markets.

articles.title: MetaX and UBTech-backed robotics chip startup Xilect raises RMB 500 million
articles.snippet: MetaX and UBTech-backed robotics chip startup Xilect raises RMB 500 million TechNode
articles.text:
Xilect, a robotics chip startup jointly founded by Chinese GPU maker MetaX and humanoid robot maker UBTech Robotics, has raised RMB 500 million in an angel round. The company will use the funding to develop its first chip and supporting software, expand its engineering team and test the platform with robot manufacturers.
Xilect is designing a system-on-chip that combines multimodal perception, decision-making and motion control on the robot itself. Its software toolchain is intended to help robot makers run existing AI models on the platform. The startup plans to give partners a development and testing platform in 2027 and release its first chip in 2028. [ Xilect , in Chinese]

Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 7:36 AM
Google: Gemini 4 Hydrogen Launches With Faster Agentic AI, 1 Million-Token Context Window, And New Multi-Model Orchestration
Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new artificial intelligence model designed to deliver faster execution, improved reasoning, and greater efficiency across software development, enterprise workflows, and everyday AI applications. The model features a 1 million-token context window, four adjustable reasoning levels, and expanded capabilities for autonomous AI agents, while Google is also introducing a multi-model orchestration system that coordinates different Gemini models within a single workflow.
Announced on November 12, 2026, Gemini 4 Hydrogen joins Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon models, which are designed for more demanding reasoning tasks.
While Carbon and Argon focus on complex problems requiring deeper analysis, Hydrogen emphasizes rapid execution across coding, research, data analysis, and other agentic workflows.
Google is making Hydrogen available across Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and Google Antigravity for eligible paid subscribers.
The company has priced Hydrogen at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, with flat pricing across its entire 1 million-token context window.
Google says Hydrogen achieves a score of 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high reasoning setting, compared with 50 for Gemini 4 Argon. Hydrogen reaches 54 at its highest reasoning setting, known as xhigh.
New Orchestrator Coordinates Multiple Gemini Models
One of the most significant additions accompanying Hydrogen is Orchestrator, a new capability within Google Antigravity that dynamically switches between AI models during a single development session.
The technology is designed to use different models for different stages of a task rather than relying on one model throughout an entire workflow.
For example, Gemini 4 Carbon can handle complex architectural decisions or coordinate a development project, while Hydrogen performs code generation, testing, debugging, and verification.
Google says this approach allows developers to combine the reasoning capabilities of its frontier models with Hydrogen’s execution efficiency.
In Terminal-Bench 4.0 testing, Orchestrator achieved task success rates approaching those of Carbon while consuming an average of 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster.
The system also supports parallel AI agents operating across isolated workspaces.
These agents can work simultaneously on different parts of a software development project, potentially reducing execution time and resource consumption.
Google believes this multi-model approach can help organizations optimize AI workloads based on task complexity, latency requirements, and operating costs.
Major Improvements Over Gemini 3.8 Flash
Hydrogen represents a significant upgrade over Google’s previous Gemini 3.8 Flash model.
At its default high reasoning setting, Hydrogen completes tasks approximately 2.5 times faster while improving its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score from 18.2% to 57%, according to Google’s evaluations.
The company also reported that Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than fivefold compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash.

articles.text:
Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 4:15 PM
Erie Strategic Ventures: Investments In Blitzy And HiddenLayer To Advance Enterprise AI Infrastructure And Security
Erie Strategic Ventures, the corporate venture capital arm of Erie Insurance, has announced investments in Blitzy and HiddenLayer, two technology companies focused on enterprise AI infrastructure, software modernization, and artificial intelligence security. The investments expand Erie Strategic Ventures’ portfolio of companies developing technologies that can help organizations deploy, manage, and secure AI applications.
Blitzy provides an autonomous software development platform designed to modernize large enterprise codebases through coordinated AI agents. HiddenLayer develops security technology that protects generative, predictive, and agentic AI systems throughout their lifecycles.
The investments reflect Erie Insurance’s continued exploration of AI technologies that could support its operations, independent insurance agents, and policyholders.
Erie Strategic Ventures was launched in August 2022 to invest in companies operating across the personal and commercial insurance value chain, as well as adjacent technology markets.
The venture capital program is operated with support from Cerity Partners Ventures, which helps corporations manage strategic investment initiatives.
Through the program, Erie Insurance combines capital investment with opportunities for technology collaboration and business development.
Blitzy Focuses On Autonomous Software Development
Blitzy develops an AI-powered software engineering platform intended to help enterprises modernize legacy systems and accelerate new application development.
The company’s technology uses a proprietary ontology and graph-based architecture to develop a detailed understanding of large software codebases.
This approach is designed to provide AI systems with contextual information about how applications, components, and dependencies interact.
Using that information, Blitzy coordinates thousands of AI agents operating in parallel to perform software development tasks.
The platform is intended to address challenges associated with maintaining and updating complex enterprise software environments.
Large organizations frequently operate systems that have accumulated years of modifications, integrations, and dependencies.
Modernizing these environments can require significant engineering resources because changes to one component may affect other applications or business processes.
Blitzy’s approach seeks to improve efficiency by enabling AI agents to analyze software architecture and coordinate development activities.
The company also supports the creation of new software products, allowing engineering teams to use autonomous agents for development workflows.
For insurance companies and other financial services organizations, software modernization can be particularly important because many essential business processes depend on established technology systems.
Erie Strategic Ventures’ investment provides exposure to technology intended to improve enterprise software development and infrastructure management.
